plan: [I will bid my value. This is because, in the ascending clock auction, I want to stay in as long as the price is below my value. By bidding my value, I ensure that I exit the auction exactly when the clock reaches my value. If I bid lower than my value, I might exit too early and miss out on a profitable opportunity. If I bid higher than my value, I risk winning at a price higher than my value, resulting in a loss. Therefore, bidding my true value is the optimal strategy.]

[My value is $35. I want to win if the second-highest bid is less than my value, and lose otherwise. I should bid a little less than my value to ensure a profit if I win, but not so low that I lose out on potential profit. A bid of $34.50 seems reasonable. This allows me to win if the other bids are lower, and I still make a profit. ]

[I will bid my true value. This is because if I bid lower, I risk exiting the auction prematurely and missing out on potential profit. If I bid higher, I risk winning the auction at a price that exceeds my value, resulting in a loss. Bidding my true value ensures that I only win the auction if the final price is less than or equal to my value, maximizing my potential profit.]
